data.reasoning: Both models reviewed the same 4 files (PKGBUILD, .SRCINFO, LICENSE, .gitignore) and found no malicious code. The PKGBUILD is a standard Rust package build with pinned source (tagged GitHub release v0.2.0) and b2sum checksum verification. The .SRCINFO contains standard metadata with no suspicious operations. The LICENSE is a standard ISC license. The .gitignore is a standard AUR .gitignore file. No injection patterns, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts. The only disagreement was due to an API error in qwen3-235b when reviewing .gitignore, which deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed and found safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in qwen3-235b when attempting to review .gitignore, resulting in an inconclusive verdict for that file and thus the overall package. deepseek-v4-flash successfully reviewed the same file and found it to be a standard AUR .gitignore with no security issues. This is a tool failure, not a substantive disagreement about security.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b failed to review .gitignore due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError), causing an inconclusive verdict
learnings: API errors on non-executable files (like .gitignore) should not cause the entire audit to be marked inconclusive when another model successfully reviews the file and finds it safe. The adjudication logic should recognize tool failures vs substantive security disagreements.
When multiple models are used, the system should track which files each model successfully reviewed and use successful reviews to resolve inconclusive verdicts caused by API errors on the same files.

Both models correctly identified standard AUR packaging patterns (cargo fetch, environment variable exports, pinned sources with checksums) without flagging false positives, indicating good prompt calibration for Rust packages.
